thread.title: Apple, FANG Lead These 3 Market-Beating Tech Stock Plays

author: NANCY GONDO
title: Apple, FANG Lead These 3 Market-Beating Tech Stock Plays
text:
Tech stocks endured a beating Monday as Invesco QQQ Trust ( QQQ ) tumbled 2.3%, weighed down by big declines in the FANG stocks.
X But they rebounded Tuesday, helping several tech-focused exchange traded funds find support near their 50-day moving average lines. A solid bounce off the line could mark a potential buy opportunity, but with the market uptrend under pressure, all purchases are at greater risk than usual.
First Trust Cloud Computing ( SKYY ) got close to its 50-day line Monday after three straight declines. Tuesday, the ETF posted a 0.8% gain. The $1.6 billion fund tracks the ISE Cloud Computing Index. Its holdings are classified in three segments: pure-play cloud computing companies, those that provide goods and services to support cloud computing, and conglomerates that indirectly use or support use of cloud computing technology.
Top holdings as of June 25 included NetApp ( NTAP ), Leaderboard stock Netflix ( NFLX ), Equinix ( EQIX ) and VMware ( VMW ). The rest of the FANG stocks: Facebook ( FB ), Amazon ( AMZN ) and Alphabet ( GOOGL ) also make the top 10. Apple, which is sometimes included in the expanded FAANG stocks, belongs in the 40-stock portfolio too. Apple ( AAPL ), which breached its 50-day line Monday, staged a rebound off the support line Tuesday.

Its 15.6% year-to-date return through June 25, according to Morningstar Inc., beats the S&P 500's 2.6% gain. Average annual returns of 20.8% and 21.1% over the past three and five years, respectively, also outpace the S&P 500's 11.2% and 13.7% returns for those same periods. The ETF charges a 0.60% expense ratio.
Topped By Apple SPDR Technology ( XLK ) closed below its 50-day line Monday, but regained the line Tuesday. The $21.7 billion fund, which tracks the S&P Technology Select Sector Index, is up 9.1% this year. Software accounted for the biggest sector weight as of June 25 at 22% of assets. Internet software and services followed at about 19%, IT services 16%, technology hardware storage and peripherals 16%, and semiconductors and semiconductor equipment 15%.
Its top holdings were Apple, Microsoft ( MSFT ), Facebook and Alphabet (class C and A shares). Those five stocks made up nearly 44% of the 74-stock portfolio. XLK boasts respective average annual returns for the past three and five years of 19.6% and 20%. It carries a 0.13% expense ratio.
IShares U.S. Technology ( IYW ) also rebounded off its 50-day line Tuesday. The $4.1 billion fund, which tracks the Dow Jones U.S. Technology Index, has returned 10.2% YTD. Software and services accounted for 55% of assets, tech hardware and equipment 25%, and semiconductors and semiconductor equipment 19%. Its top five holdings were the same as XLK. They represented 51% of the 137-stock portfolio.
ITW's average annual returns over the past three and five years are 19.5% and 20.9%, respectively. The ETF charges a 0.44% expense ratio.
